EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure
paper.tldr: Experiments on three different Gaussian avatar reconstruction methods show improvements in both perceptual and reconstruction measures over the raw outputs and an SDEdit-style refinement baseline, which indicates a useful operating regime for recoverable appearance artifacts.

paper.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
paper.tldr: This work develops a fast visibility-aware rendering algorithm that supports anisotropic splatting and both accelerates training and allows realtime rendering and demonstrates state-of-the-art visual quality and real-time rendering on several established datasets.

paper.title: GaussianAvatars: Photorealistic Head Avatars with Rigged 3D Gaussians
paper.tldr: This work introduces GaussianAvatars11, a new method to create photorealistic head avatars that are fully controllable in terms of expression, pose, and viewpoint and jointly optimize for the morphable model parameters and Gaussian splat parameters in an end-to-end fashion.

paper.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
paper.tldr: High quality image synthesis results are presented using diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models inspired by considerations from nonequilibrium thermodynamics, which naturally admit a progressive lossy decompression scheme that can be interpreted as a generalization of autoregressive decoding.

Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Second Workshop for REsearch on Agent Language Models (REALM 2026)
paper.tldr: This work investigates whether open-weight models can generate less verbose reasoning by changing the form of their own earlier thoughts, without retraining, and identifies reasoning history as one way to reduce future reasoning-token use and motivate model-specific compaction policies evaluated for both efficiency and retained capability.

paper.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
paper.tldr: This work proposes LiveCodeBench, a comprehensive and contamination-free evaluation of LLMs for code, which continuously collects new problems over time from contests across three competition platforms, namely LeetCode, AtCoder, and CodeForces.

paper.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
paper.tldr: SWE-bench is introduced, an evaluation framework consisting of software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests across popular Python repositories that shows that both state-of-the-art proprietary models and the fine-tuned model SWE-Llama can resolve only the simplest issues.

paper.title: SEAL: Steerable Reasoning Calibration of Large Language Models for Free
paper.tldr: This work investigates the internal reasoning structures of LLMs and categorizes them into three primary thought types: execution, reflection, and transition thoughts, and introduces SEAL (Steerable reasoning calibration), a training-free approach that seamlessly calibrates the CoT process, improving accuracy while demonstrating significant efficiency gains.
